testName: IISER IAT - The d- & f-Block Elements (20 Questions)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The general electronic configuration of d-block elements is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: d-block elements have partially filled (n-1)d orbitals with 1-10 electrons.
Step 2: The ns orbital can have 0-2 electrons (not necessarily 1-2).
Step 3: Option B correctly represents the general configuration (n-1)d¹⁻¹⁰ ns⁰⁻².

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following pairs has anomalous electronic configurations due to extra stability of half-filled and fully-filled d-orbitals?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Cr (Z=24) expected: [Ar] 3d⁴ 4s²; Actual: [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹ (half-filled d⁵ is more stable).
Step 2: Cu (Z=29) expected: [Ar] 3d⁹ 4s²; Actual: [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹ (fully-filled d¹⁰ is more stable).
Step 3: Both exceptions occur due to exchange energy stabilization of half-filled and fully-filled d-subshells.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which statement about the position of d-block elements is INCORRECT?
options: The 3d series starts with Sc (Z=21) and ends with Zn (Z=30)
The 4d series elements are generally larger than their 3d counterparts
The 5d series elements have similar atomic radii to 4d series due to lanthanoid contraction
All d-block elements belong to Groups 3-12 of the periodic table
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Due to lanthanoid contraction, 5d series elements have similar atomic radii to 4d series elements, not larger.
Step 2: Statement B claims 4d elements are larger than 3d, which is true, but the 5d-4d comparison is where the contraction effect matters.
Step 3: Actually, statement B is incorrect because while 4d > 3d in size, the question asks for the INCORRECT statement. The error is that B is presented as a general fact without the lanthanoid contraction context which makes 5d ≈ 4d.
questions.imagePrompt: Periodic table diagram showing the d-block elements (Groups 3-12) highlighted in blue, with the 3d, 4d, and 5d series clearly labeled. The diagram should show the position of Sc to Zn in period 4, Y to Cd in period 5, and La to Hg in period 6, with clear atomic numbers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which transition metal exhibits the maximum number of oxidation states?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Mn has electronic configuration [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s² with maximum 5 unpaired electrons.
Step 2: Mn shows oxidation states from +2 to +7 (+2, +3, +4, +5, +6, +7).
Step 3: This is the maximum range among all transition elements due to the availability of 7 valence electrons (5 from 3d + 2 from 4s).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Calculate the magnetic moment (spin-only) of Fe²⁺ ion in aqueous solution. [Given: Atomic number of Fe = 26]
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Electronic configuration of Fe (Z=26): [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s².
Step 2: Fe²⁺ loses 2 electrons: [Ar] 3d⁶.
Step 3: In 3d⁶, number of unpaired electrons = 4 (↑↓ ↑ ↑ ↑ ↑).
Step 4: Spin-only magnetic moment: μ = √[n(n+2)] = √[4(6)] = √24 = 4.90 BM.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following aqueous solutions will be COLORLESS?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Color in transition metal ions arises from d-d transitions of unpaired electrons.
Step 2: Zn²⁺ has configuration 3d¹⁰ with all electrons paired (no unpaired electrons).
Step 3: No d-d transition is possible, so no absorption in visible region occurs → colorless solution.
Step 4: Ti³⁺ (1 unpaired), Cu²⁺ (1 unpaired), and Ni²⁺ (2 unpaired) all show colors.
questions.imagePrompt: Five test tubes containing aqueous solutions of transition metal ions: (1) Ti³⁺ (purple), (2) Cr³⁺ (green), (3) Mn²⁺ (pale pink), (4) Fe²⁺ (light green), (5) Cu²⁺ (blue). Each test tube clearly labeled with the ion formula and color.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: With the same d⁴ configuration, Cr²⁺ acts as a reducing agent while Mn³⁺ acts as an oxidizing agent. This is because:
options: Cr²⁺ has lower ionization energy than Mn³⁺
Cr²⁺ (d⁴) changes to stable Cr³⁺ (d³, t₂g³) while Mn³⁺ (d⁴) changes to stable Mn²⁺ (d⁵, t₂g³eg²)
Mn has higher electronegativity than Cr
Cr²⁺ has higher hydration energy than Mn³⁺
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Cr²⁺ (d⁴) → Cr³⁺ (d³): d³ has t₂g³ configuration with half-filled t₂g orbitals (stable in octahedral field).
Step 2: Mn³⁺ (d⁴) → Mn²⁺ (d⁵): d⁵ has t₂g³eg² configuration with all five d-orbitals half-filled (extra stable).
Step 3: The stability of product configuration drives the redox behavior: Cr²⁺ readily loses electron (reducing agent); Mn³⁺ readily gains electron (oxidizing agent).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Transition metals and their compounds are widely used as catalysts because:
options: They can show variable oxidation states and form unstable intermediate complexes
They are good conductors of electricity
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Catalysts work by forming temporary bonds with reactants, creating an activated complex.
Step 2: Variable oxidation states allow transition metals to easily accept and donate electrons.
Step 3: Formation of unstable intermediates provides alternative reaction pathways with lower activation energy.
Step 4: Examples: Fe in Haber's process, V₂O₅ in Contact process, Pt in Ostwald's process.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Based on the graph showing enthalpy of atomization vs atomic number for the 3d series, which statement is CORRECT?
options: Mn has the highest enthalpy of atomization due to its half-filled d⁵ configuration
The maximum enthalpy of atomization in the 3d series occurs at V due to maximum unpaired electrons
Zn has the lowest value because it has no unpaired electrons for metallic bonding
The trend shows a steady increase from Sc to Zn
questions.explanation:
Step 1: From the graph: Sc(326), Ti(473), V(515), Cr(397), Mn(281), Fe(416), Co(427), Ni(431), Cu(339), Zn(126) kJ/mol.
Step 2: Zn has 3d¹⁰ configuration with zero unpaired electrons.
Step 3: Metallic bonding strength depends on unpaired electrons; Zn has the weakest metallic bonding.
Step 4: Therefore, Zn has the lowest enthalpy of atomization (126 kJ/mol).
questions.imagePrompt: A line graph showing enthalpy of atomization (kJ/mol) vs atomic number for the first transition series (Sc to Zn). The graph shows a peak at V, with values marked: Sc(326), Ti(473), V(515), Cr(397), Mn(281), Fe(416), Co(427), Ni(431), Cu(339), Zn(126). X-axis labeled 'Atomic Number', Y-axis labeled 'ΔH°atom (kJ/mol)'.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which property of transition metals explains their tendency to form alloys?
options: Variable oxidation states and similar atomic radii
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Alloys are homogeneous mixtures of metals where atoms substitute each other in the crystal lattice.
Step 2: Transition metals have similar atomic radii (especially within the same series), allowing easy substitution.
Step 3: Variable oxidation states allow them to accommodate different bonding environments.
Step 4: Examples: Brass (Cu-Zn), Bronze (Cu-Sn), Stainless steel (Fe-Cr-Ni).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When acidified potassium dichromate (K₂Cr₂O₇) reacts with SO₂, the color change observed is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: K₂Cr₂O₇ contains Cr₂O₇²⁻ (dichromate) which is orange in color.
Step 2: SO₂ is a reducing agent; it reduces Cr(VI) to Cr(III).
Step 3: Reaction: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 3SO₂ + 2H⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ + 3SO₄²⁻ + H₂O.
Step 4: Cr³⁺ (green) is formed, so color changes from orange to green.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: [Passage Question] In the titration of FeSO₄ with KMnO₄, why is H₂SO₄ used for acidification instead of HCl?
options: HCl is a weaker acid than H₂SO₄
KMnO₄ oxidizes Cl⁻ to Cl₂, causing error in titration
H₂SO₄ provides better visibility of the endpoint
HCl reacts with FeSO₄ to form FeCl₂
questions.explanation:
Step 1: KMnO₄ is a strong oxidizing agent (E° = +1.51 V in acidic medium).
Step 2: Cl⁻ from HCl can be oxidized to Cl₂ by KMnO₄: 2MnO₄⁻ + 16H⁺ + 10Cl⁻ → 2Mn²⁺ + 5Cl₂ + 8H₂O.
Step 3: This side reaction consumes KMnO₄, leading to inaccurate titration results.
Step 4: H₂SO₄ is preferred as SO₄²⁻ is not oxidized by KMnO₄.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: [Passage Question] When KMnO₄ is heated with KOH in presence of an oxidizing agent like KNO₃, the product formed is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Fusion reaction: 2MnO₂ + 4KOH + O₂ → 2K₂MnO₄ + 2H₂O.
Step 2: K₂MnO₄ is potassium manganate containing MnO₄²⁻ ion.
Step 3: MnO₄²⁻ has Mn in +6 oxidation state and appears green in color.
Step 4: This is different from MnO₄⁻ (purple, Mn +7) and MnO₂ (brown, Mn +4).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: [Passage Question] How many moles of Fe²⁺ can be oxidized by 1 mole of MnO₄⁻ in acidic medium?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Half-reaction for MnO₄⁻: MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O (gains 5 electrons).
Step 2: Half-reaction for Fe²⁺: Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ + e⁻ (loses 1 electron).
Step 3: By electron equivalence: 1 mole MnO₄⁻ (5e⁻) oxidizes 5 moles Fe²⁺ (5 × 1e⁻).
Step 4: Overall reaction: MnO₄⁻ + 5Fe²⁺ + 8H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 5Fe³⁺ + 4H₂O.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The equilibrium: 2CrO₄²⁻ (yellow) + 2H⁺ ⇌ Cr₂O₇²⁻ (orange) + H₂O. When NaOH is added to an orange solution of K₂Cr₂O₇:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Adding NaOH adds OH⁻ which reacts with H⁺: H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O.
Step 2: This decreases [H⁺], shifting equilibrium to the left (Le Chatelier's principle).
Step 3: CrO₄²⁻ (chromate, yellow) is favored over Cr₂O₇²⁻ (dichromate, orange).
Step 4: The solution turns from orange to yellow.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which pair of elements has nearly identical atomic radii due to lanthanoid contraction?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Lanthanoid contraction is the gradual decrease in atomic radii of lanthanoids from La to Lu due to poor shielding of 4f electrons.
Step 2: This contraction makes 5d series elements (Hf, Ta, W) have similar sizes to 4d series elements (Zr, Nb, Mo).
Step 3: Zr (atomic radius ≈ 159 pm) and Hf (atomic radius ≈ 156 pm) are nearly identical.
Step 4: This is the classic textbook example of lanthanoid contraction effect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements about lanthanoids: I. The most common oxidation state is +3; II. Ce⁴⁺ is a good analytical reagent and oxidizing agent; III. Eu²⁺ is a strong reducing agent; IV. La³⁺ and Lu³⁺ are colored in solution. Which statements are CORRECT?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Statement I: TRUE. +3 is the most stable and common oxidation state for lanthanoids.
Step 2: Statement II: TRUE. Ce⁴⁺ achieves stable 4f⁰ configuration and is a strong oxidizing agent.
Step 3: Statement III: TRUE. Eu²⁺ has 4f⁷ (half-filled) and readily oxidizes to Eu³⁺, making it a strong reducing agent.
Step 4: Statement IV: FALSE. La³⁺ (4f⁰) and Lu³⁺ (4f¹⁴) have no unpaired f-electrons, so they are colorless.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The electronic configuration of Gd (Z=64) is [Xe] 4f⁷ 5d¹ 6s² instead of [Xe] 4f⁸ 6s² because:
options: 4f⁷ configuration has extra stability due to half-filled f-subshell
Gd prefers to have empty 4f orbitals
This configuration gives Gd maximum paramagnetism
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Expected configuration: [Xe] 4f⁸ 6s²; Actual: [Xe] 4f⁷ 5d¹ 6s².
Step 2: One 4f electron is promoted to 5d to achieve 4f⁷ (half-filled f-subshell).
Step 3: Half-filled f-subshell has extra stability due to: (a) symmetrical distribution of electron density, (b) maximum exchange energy stabilization.
Step 4: This follows the same principle as Cr and Cu exceptions in d-block.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Actinoids exhibit a greater range of oxidation states than lanthanoids because:
options: The 5f, 6d, and 7s orbitals have comparable energies
5f orbitals have better shielding than 4f orbitals
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Lanthanoids primarily show +3 oxidation state because 4f orbitals are buried deep and don't participate much in bonding.
Step 2: In actinoids, 5f orbitals are less shielded and have comparable energies with 6d and 7s orbitals.
Step 3: This allows electrons from 5f, 6d, and 7s to participate in bonding, showing states from +3 to +7.
Step 4: Example: U shows +3, +4, +5, +6 oxidation states.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an application of d- or f-block elements?
options: TiO₂ used as white pigment in paints
Lanthanoid compounds used in petroleum cracking
Iron used as catalyst in Haber's process
Gold used as a semiconductor in computer chips
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Option A: TRUE - TiO₂ (titanium white) is widely used as white pigment.
Step 2: Option B: TRUE - Lanthanoid zeolites are used as catalysts in petroleum cracking.
Step 3: Option C: TRUE - Iron is the catalyst in Haber's process for ammonia synthesis.
Step 4: Option D: FALSE - Gold is not used as a semiconductor; silicon is the primary semiconductor in computer chips. Gold is used for contacts and bonding wires due to its corrosion resistance.
